For each request, `BaseHandler.get_response`, or `BaseHandler.get_response_async`, sets it to `settings.ROOT_URLCONF` before it calls the middleware chain, and when the response is closed, `reset_urlconf`, a receiver of `request_finished` that the handler's module connects, unsets it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:reset_urlconf`).

A middleware sets an attribute named `"urlconf"` on the request, and when the request reaches the centre of the chain `BaseHandler.resolve_request` finds the attribute, makes that URLconf the current one, and resolves with its resolver (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).
The `process_view` hooks are called after `resolve_request`, and find the new one (`docs/ref/request-response.txt`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).
The `process_view` hooks are called after `resolve_request`, and find the new one (`docs/ref/request-response.txt`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

Because `resolve_request` makes the URLconf current, and does not merely resolve with it, the rest of the request agrees with it: the view reverses by the members' names, and had it raised, with `settings.DEBUG` off, the error view would have been looked for in the members' URLconf module, since the handler asks for the resolver of the current URLconf when it needs one ([From a URLconf to a tree](urlconf.md#what-else-a-urlconf-module-may-hold)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
`_prefixes` and `_urlconfs` are each a `Local` from asgiref, an object whose attributes hold a value for each thread (`asgiref:asgiref/local.py:Local`).

The `Local` keeps a value with the asynchronous context it was set in, and asgiref's docstring gives its reach: code awaited from the frame that set the value sees it, and so do tasks started from there and synchronous code that `sync_to_async` runs in a thread (`asgiref:asgiref/local.py:Local`).

So a view that is a plain function, which the ASGI handler runs on a worker thread, reads its request's prefix and URLconf; and the way back is open too: `reset_urlconf`, run on the worker thread as the response is closed, leaves the URLconf unset for the coroutine that awaited the handler as well (`asgiref:asgiref/sync.py:SyncToAsync.__call__`).

Within Django it has one caller, `root_urlconf_changed`, a receiver of `setting_changed` that the test framework connects: when a test overrides `ROOT_URLCONF`, it clears the caches and unsets the current URLconf, as the override begins and again as it ends, so the root resolver found after an override is not the one there was before it ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md#the-receivers-of-setting_changed)) (`django/urls/base.py:clear_url_caches`, `django/test/signals.py:root_urlconf_changed`).
